findings: The deep step (rotation parts of elements of a discrete Gamma near 1 commute) is proved ELEMENTARILY, with the uniform epsilon = 1/64 (independent of Gamma, v0, d), and without ellipticity: (a) Zassenhaus halving in a normed ring, ||X^{±1}-1|| <= 1/32, ||Y^{±1}-1|| <= m <= 3 => ||[X,Y]^{±1}-1|| <= m/2; (b) Engel property: conjugating the affine extensions (y,s) -> (L y + s tau, s) by the flag scaling D_K = sum K^i P_i (flag R v0 ⊂ v0^perp ⊂ M^n ⊂ M^n x R, all affine maps with L v0 = v0 block upper triangular with diagonal (1, rho, 1, 1)) makes g^{±1} 1/32-close and h^{±1} 3-close to 1, so iterated commutators [g,[g,...,h]] -> 1 and discreteness makes them 1; (c) Frobenius: rho(A) commuting with rho(B A B^-1), ||rho(B)-1|| < 1/2 => c = [rho A, rho B] has all powers within 2||rho B - 1|| < 1 of 1, and no small subgroups (von Neumann's mean ergodic theorem on the screen) gives c = 1; (d) backward induction along the iterated commutators. Neither Auslander's theorem, Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem, the structure of compact groups, nor Tits' alternative is needed — the earlier obstruction ('mathlib has no Lie groups') was a property of the route, not of the statement.

Consequently TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d is a theorem for every d with no sorry and no external; Theorems A/B of Flat/Classification no longer inherit a sorry through titsVirtuallyAbelianNull (their docstrings, and Flat/Nonloxodromic's l.25-27/96-98/116, still say 'one tagged sorry' and should be updated by the master session; this package does not edit them).

The free quaternion pair of Nonloxodromic finding (7) remains consistent: there rho(Gamma) is dense in a copy of SU(2), and the Gamma is not discrete; discreteness is spent at exactly one point (step 4(b)).

Barbot's 'natural action of L(Gamma)' on P0bar (l.2627-2629) is realised as rho(A) = pi A pi + (1 - pi); it acts as (t, y) -> (t, R y) with R orthogonal (fst_screenRot_apply, norm_screenRot_apply), i.e. it is an isometry of the sup norm of Minkowski d.

kb_proposals: A quotient like Barbot's P0bar = v0^perp / R v0 is cheapest as a SECTION: the screen {v0, e0}^perp with Submodule.projection, and the induced action as the unital endomorphism pi A pi + (1 - pi) of M^n -- multiplicative on the stabiliser, normed for free (CausalScaffold.Flat.TitsNull).

Finite index by compactness: a bounded 'almost-homomorphism into a proper normed ring' gives finite index of the subgroup generated by the eps-near-1 elements (relIndex_closure_ne_zero, pigeonhole through Metric.totallyBounded_iff and QuotientGroup.out_eq').

Zassenhaus/Bieberbach contraction without Lie theory: if every element is block upper triangular in a flag with isometric diagonal blocks, conjugate by the scaling D_K = sum K^i P_i (CausalScaffold.Flat.TitsNull: scaleBy, norm_scaleBy_conj_sub_le); for K large the elements are close to their diagonal, and the normed-ring halving lemma norm_commutator_le_half applies.

No small subgroups in O(n) is one call to the mean ergodic theorem: ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_orthogonalProjection (import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.MeanErgodic); see eq_self_of_forall_iterate_near.

Heartbeat pitfall: a single theorem manipulating many ‖·‖ of continuous linear maps on Minkowski d × ℝ exhausts the 200000 heartbeats in typeclass inference (reported as 'timeout at whnf' on the declaration line, not at the culprit); split it into lemmas. Also, `set x := …` followed by `positivity`/`rw` on a goal mentioning x can force whnf of the set body; prefer explicit positivity facts or `clear_value`.
